problem_context: Current generative modeling approaches face fundamental challenges in mapping from one distribution to another efficiently. While discriminative models focus on mapping individual samples to labels, generative models must learn mappings between entire distributions - a significantly more complex task. Existing methods often require iterative procedures at inference time, performing multiple network evaluations to progressively transform samples from noise to data. This creates a fundamental tension: decomposing complex transformations into simpler steps improves feasibility but increases computational cost at generation time. There is a need for generative models that can produce high-quality samples in a single forward pass while maintaining the modeling capacity to capture complex data distributions.
desirable_properties: Should generate high-quality samples in a single network evaluation
Should scale effectively to high-resolution, complex data distributions
Should avoid mode collapse and capture the full diversity of the target distribution
Should provide a principled training objective without requiring adversarial optimization
Should work across different data modalities beyond just images
Should support conditional generation with flexible conditioning mechanisms
Should achieve competitive performance with multi-step methods despite using only one step
field_context: Generative modeling is a fundamental problem in machine learning that aims to learn the underlying distribution of data and generate new samples from it. This field has seen significant progress through various paradigms including variational methods, adversarial training, normalizing flows, and iterative refinement approaches, each with distinct trade-offs between sample quality, computational efficiency, and training stability.
